gap: No result ChatGPT got states Obsessed Garage's bench figures for the two modular picks: the Active 2.3 measured 2.26 GPM at 1,005 PSI, 85 dB, and drew 17.3 A with a 1.25 mm foam cannon; the Kränzle K1322TS measured 1.97 GPM at 1,010 PSI, 68 dB, and drew 16.2 A with the same orifice. Both draws are above a 15 A circuit's rating.
standout_why: I opened Bob Vila's Grandfalls Pro review (cited) and its Yahoo syndication, ProGarageGear (cited), TOTimes (cited), the Giraffe Tools blog (cited), FixLine Local (rank 1 / rank 2 results) and CleanGearLab. None of them gives a measurement with the measurer named. Bob Vila took no readings: it lists PSI and '78-80 dB' as specs only. ProGarageGear gives about 82 dB for the Active 2.0 and about 70 dB for the Kränzle as 'manufacturer and reviewer figures' with no source, and its Grandfalls '1.2–1.8 real-world' GPM has no stated method. TOTimes repeats Giraffe's published dB. FixLine and CleanGearLab both say they have not tested anything. No page has the Active 2.3's measured flow or noise, and none has foam-cannon amp draw for any unit. Popular Mechanics (cited) blocked fetching, so I couldn't check it.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's 'Active 2.3 for car detailing' pick on flow: it measured 2.26 GPM against the Kränzle's 1.97 GPM, at the same roughly 1,000 PSI. It also adds two costs that ChatGPT left out. The Active measured 17 dB louder (85 vs 68 dB), which matters in an enclosed garage, and on a foam cannon both units drew more than 15 A. So a garage that only has a 15 A GFCI outlet would need a 20 A circuit before running either modular setup with foam. That makes the all-in-one Grandfalls easier to recommend for most garages. None of Giraffe's units has a published measurement, so the page should say that its PSI and dB figures are Giraffe's own claims.
